title: Function identity for noised coordinate restrictions
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, $f\colon\{0,1\}^{n+1}\to\mathbb{R}$, $\rho\in\mathbb{R}$, and $b\in\{0,1\}$. Write $f_b(x)=f(x,b)$, $a_f(x)=\tfrac12(f(x,0)+f(x,1))$, $d_f(x)=\tfrac12(f(x,0)-f(x,1))$, and let $\sigma(0)=1$, $\sigma(1)=-1$. As functions on $\{0,1\}^n$, $T_\rho f_b=T_\rho a_f+\sigma(b)T_\rho d_f$.
replaced: Let $T_\rho$ denote Boolean noise with real correlation $\rho$, whose Fourier multiplier on a set of size $k$ is $\rho^k$. For $f:\{0,1\}^{n+1}\to\mathbb R$, put $f_b(x)=f(x,b)$, $a_f=(f_0+f_1)/2$, and $d_f=(f_0-f_1)/2$, and let $s_0=1$, $s_1=-1$. For either bit $b$, $T_\rho f_b=T_\rho a_f+s_bT_\rho d_f$ as functions on $\{0,1\}^n$.
